code.database.graph.why: Store property graph data and answer Cypher queries over it from inside the analyst process, with no database server.
code.database.graph.how: Opens an embedded database, runs Cypher through a connection and returns typed rows.

code.database.graph.why: Load hundreds of thousands of rows into the graph in minutes rather than hours.
code.database.graph.how: Accepts COPY statements from CSV or Parquet files and Arrow record batches registered as tables.

code.database.graph.why: Place table partitions on other hosts while the engine stays unaware of distribution.
code.database.graph.how: Exposes placement, lifecycle and row-insert hooks for partitioned node tables.

upstream.library.database.why: Reach the C++ engine classes (database, connection, query result, value) from safe Rust.
upstream.library.database.how: Declares cxx bindings that a C++ shim in lbug_rs.cpp implements over the engine API.

upstream.archive.prebuilt.why: Obtain a linkable liblbug and its headers without compiling the engine.
upstream.archive.prebuilt.how: Runs scripts/download_lbug.sh to fetch the compat or perf static archive for the host platform into a cache.

upstream.library.database.why: Fall back to compiling the engine when no archive can be downloaded, or when LBUG_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE is set.
upstream.library.database.how: Builds the bundled lbug-src tree with CMake and links it statically.

upstream.library.openssl.why: Link the TLS and crypto libraries the static engine needs at run time.
upstream.library.openssl.how: Finds the library directory through OPENSSL_DIR, vcpkg or pkg-config.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Convert between Rust values and engine values for query parameters, result cells and routed rows.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Maps the Value enum, NodeVal, RelVal and LogicalType to and from the C++ value and type objects; rejects read-only types.

code.error.database.why: Report a value that cannot cross the boundary.
code.error.database.how: Returns Error::ReadOnlyType or a conversion error.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Open or create the on-disk database with the chosen SystemConfig (buffer pool, threads, read-only, checkpointing, multi-write).
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls the C++ database constructor through the bridge.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Read rows, column names, column types and timings from the engine result.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Iterates the C++ result one tuple at a time.

code.codec.value.why: Present each cell as a typed Rust value.
code.codec.value.how: Yields a Vec of Value per row and prints a table through Display.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Plan a parameterised query once and run it many times.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Holds the C++ prepared statement and reports whether it is read-only.

code.engine.database.why: Attach to an open database to run statements.
code.engine.database.how: Connection::new borrows the Database for its lifetime.

code.statement.prepared.why: Avoid planning the same query again for repeated runs.
code.statement.prepared.how: prepare returns a statement; execute binds a list of named Values.

code.result.query.why: Return the answer of each query.
code.result.query.how: query and execute return a QueryResult.

code.codec.value.how: Converts each named Value into an engine value.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Send query text and control settings (threads, timeout, interrupt).
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls connection_query, connection_prepare, connection_execute and the setters.

code.error.database.why: Report a failed query or a failed prepare.
code.error.database.how: Returns Error::FailedQuery or Error::FailedPreparedStatement with the engine message.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Move columnar data across the C++ boundary without row conversion.
code.bridge.ffi.how: A second cxx bridge (feature arrow) over lbug_arrow.cpp for create_arrow_table, create_arrow_rel_table, query_as_arrow, iter_arrow and csr.

upstream.library.arrow.why: Represent record batches and schemas in Rust.
upstream.library.arrow.how: Uses the arrow crate FFI structs as the exchanged data.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Install process-global hooks in the engine for placement, partition lifecycle and row insert.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Registers C callbacks through lbug_partition_routing.cpp; a panic aborts the process.

code.codec.value.why: Hand inserted rows to the wrapper as typed values in parent schema order.
code.codec.value.how: Decodes each row cell into a Value before calling the insert_row callback.

code.engine.database.why: Own the database files and settings.
code.engine.database.how: Database::new opens a path with a SystemConfig.

code.result.query.how: Result iterates Vec<Value> and prints as a table.

code.codec.value.how: Value enum covering scalars, lists, structs, nodes and rels.

code.script.build.why: Link the engine at build time.

code.bridge.arrow.how: Arrow tables and CSR results behind the arrow feature.

code.router.partition.why: Let a wrapper own partitions on other hosts.

specification.title: Unused public type
specification.text: CSVOptions is exported from lib.rs and has delimiter, escape_character and newline builders. No function in src/ accepts it, so a caller cannot use it. The CSV writer that took it was probably removed. The type should be removed or its consumer restored.

upstream.library.database.why: Fall back to compiling the engine when no archive can be downloaded, or when LBUG_BUILD_FROM_SOURCE is set.
upstream.library.database.how: Builds the engine with CMake and links it statically. The source root is LBUG_SOURCE_DIR, then ../ladybug, then the bundled lbug-src, then a download of the release tarball. On Linux it adds -rdynamic so extensions can resolve engine symbols.

code.bridge.ffi.why: Send query text and control settings (threads, timeout, interrupt), and plan a parameterised query once to run it many times.
code.bridge.ffi.how: Calls connection_query, connection_prepare, connection_execute and the setters. prepare returns a PreparedStatement that holds the C++ statement and reports is_read_only; execute binds named Values to it.

specification.title: Conversion failure
specification.text: The Iterator implementation of QueryResult calls unwrap on each cell conversion. A cell that cannot convert makes the iteration panic instead of returning an Error. A TODO comment in src/query_result.rs records this.

specification.title: Prepared statements
specification.text: PreparedStatement is a struct in src/connection.rs that the Connection owns the use of. The map records it in the Connection element because the purpose of the Connection (run and re-run queries) carries the statement's purpose.
